headline: One-time charge dents earnings; guidance raised
summary_short: McKesson's fiscal Q1 2027 (period ended June 30, 2026) revenue rose 8% y/y to $105.4 billion, but GAAP diluted EPS fell 18% to $5.15 on a $293 million redeemable-noncontrolling-interest charge tied to the Medical-Surgical Solutions minority sale; Adjusted EPS of $9.93 grew 20% y/y.
summary_long: Revenue growth of 8% was led by North American Pharmaceutical (+5%) and Oncology & Multispecialty (+33%, aided by acquisitions), partly offset by lower branded-pharmaceutical contributions. GAAP diluted EPS fell $1.10 y/y, driven by a $293M redemption-value charge on noncontrolling interests from the Apollo Funds minority sale in Medical-Surgical Solutions, partly offset by organic growth and the absence of last year's $189M Rite Aid bad-debt charge. Adjusted EPS rose 20% to $9.93 on operational growth and a lower share count. Operating cash flow was -$220M (vs -$918M a year ago); Free Cash Flow was -$372M. McKesson returned $2.6B to shareholders and raised the quarterly dividend 15% to $0.94/share. FY2027 Adjusted EPS guidance raised to $44.20-$45.00 from $43.80-$44.60.
